title: How to Clean Your Coffee Maker (And Other Small Kitchen Appliances)
author: Written byDawn Hammonon Sep 27, 2022
steps: Start by removing your basket. Dump the grounds into the compost bin and rinse it thoroughly or run it through the washer. Then put the filter back into the machine. Also empty the water reservoir.
Next, mix one part vinegar with one part water. Pour the vinegar mixture into the empty water reservoir.

Turn the machine on and let the vinegar run through the first steps of the process. Stop the machine about halfway through the cycle and allow it to sit for 30-60 minutes. Then complete the cycle. If you have a clean cycle on your machine, use the vinegar mixture and the clean setting. It will automatically start and stop to optimize the clean.

When the cycle ends, rinse the carafe out and clean it with soap. Then fill it again with water and dump it into the machine. Run the coffee machine through a complete cycle. Allow the water to cool for several minutes. Then dump it out and repeat the process at least two more times. If, after three cycles, the water still smells like vinegar, run it through another time or two.

Once again, allow the machine to cool. Use a standard kitchen and appliance spray, or simply a soft sponge with dish soap on it, to wipe down the exterior of the machine. Vinegar works great for wiping down stainless steel coffee makers and also for cleaning the hot plate beneath the carafe.

Repeat the cleaning process at least twice annually, or as stains and buildup occurs. They aren’t as common as they used to be, but it’s still a reliable way to make coffee.
